reading.body:
CyrusOne's Cincinnati facility publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, making it the third-largest among Ohio's eight sites with disclosed power figures and holding 18 percent of the state's declared 60.4 MW.

The facility spans 143,778 square feet with IT capacity that translates to roughly 275 racks at typical AI training density. It holds certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II compliance, positioning it for regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and federal sectors. Ohio has 77 mapped data center facilities on record, but only eight publish IT capacity, making CIN2 one of the few sites in the state with transparent power specifications.

Ohio's total published capacity of 60.4 MW places it at the lower end of AI infrastructure density compared to major compute hubs. The state's actual footprint may be larger if unmapped or undisclosed facilities exist, but available data shows no visible grid or power constraints yet announced at the facility or state level. For AI operators seeking east-of-Mississippi capacity with compliance certifications, 11 MW is neither hyperscale nor negligible, and reflects a regional market where infrastructure remains modest and mostly opaque.
